article_title: Implementation of learning by design in a synchronized online environment to teach educational robotics to inservice teachers
citation: An, H., Sung, W. & Yoon, S.Y. (2022). Implementation of learning by design in a synchronized online environment to teach educational robotics to inservice teachers. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-022-10134-8
title: Synchronized online educational robotics course for inservice teachers grounded in LBD
description: An online educational robotics course designed and implemented for inservice teachers who had little or no prior experience in teaching robotics, applying instructional design factors and teaching and facilitation strategies derived from the learning by design (LBD) framework. The course included a robotics open-ended project completed by participating teachers. The authors conclude that the study sheds light on "the design components of a robotics course grounded in LBD that are effective for preparing teachers in an online environment to implement robotics in their classrooms."
requirements: Inservice teacher participants; instructional design factors and teaching and facilitation strategies derived from the LBD framework; an open-ended robotics project.
constraints: Implemented online in a synchronized environment during fall 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic; teachers recognized constraints of learning educational robotics online.
target_learners: inservice K-12 teachers with little or no robotics teaching experience
examples: Teachers completed a robotics open-ended project and reported using case-based reasoning, sketches, trial and error, and evaluating capacity.
key_sources: An, H., Sung, W. & Yoon, S.Y. (2022). Implementation of learning by design in a synchronized online environment to teach educational robotics to inservice teachers. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-022-10134-8

article_title: Developing an Instrument to Measure Public Health Nurses' Competence Related to Breastfeeding Beyond 12 Months.
citation: Pöyhönen, N., Ojantausta, O., Kaunonen, M., Vehviläinen-Julkunen, K., & Ikonen, R. (2024). Developing an Instrument to Measure Public Health Nurses’ Competence Related to Breastfeeding Beyond 12 Months. Journal of Human Lactation. https://doi.org/10.1177/08903344241254343
title: Long-Term Breastfeeding Competence Scale (LBCS)
description: The LBCS is an instrument measuring health professionals' competence — knowledge, skills, and attitudes — regarding breastfeeding beyond 12 months. It was developed from the Extended Breastfeeding Knowledge and Attitudes tool (Cockerham-Colas et al., 2012), translated into Finnish, and complemented with six new knowledge and skills items operationalized from a systematic review. The pilot version contained "a knowledge and skills dimension and an attitude dimension," with 10 knowledge/skills items and 25 attitude items; the validated instrument retains 9 and 22 items respectively. The full scale is included in the article's online Supplemental Material.
requirements: Respondents must be qualified public health nurses currently working in maternity and/or child health clinics, as in the pilot sample
constraints: The LBCS was validated in the Finnish healthcare context; the authors state that if using the LBCS in another context, its validity must be reassessed
target_learners: Public health nurses working in maternity and child health clinics
target_learning_goals: Clinical competence (knowledge, skills, attitudes) in breastfeeding counseling beyond 12 months
examples: Piloted with 197 Finnish public health nurses via a cross-sectional online survey using the RedCap tool
key_sources: Pöyhönen, N., Ojantausta, O., Kaunonen, M., Vehviläinen-Julkunen, K., & Ikonen, R. (2024). Developing an Instrument to Measure Public Health Nurses’ Competence Related to Breastfeeding Beyond 12 Months. Journal of Human Lactation. https://doi.org/10.1177/08903344241254343
